subject: City Councilor Platform and Policy Mandate
overview: Councilor Anna Callahan discussed her background in anti-corruption advocacy, the influence of corporate lobbying on local housing policy, and her commitment to the progressive platform that won a majority in the 2023 election.

items.title: Introductions and Local Favorites
items.summary: Councilor Anna Callahan introduced herself as a new city official and shared her favorite local dining locations.

items.title: Political Values and Systemic Corruption
items.summary: Callahan discussed her focus on systemic corruption and the pressure on politicians to favor wealthy interests, noting a recent motion regarding a city audit.

items.title: Real Estate Lobbying and Housing Fees
items.summary: The discussion addressed opposition from the Greater Boston Real Estate Board toward the real estate transfer fee and the distinction between corporate developers and small landlords.

items.title: Council Decorum and Electoral Mandate
items.summary: Callahan argued that electing a council majority with a shared platform provided a clear policy mandate and advocated for more respectful discourse during public meetings.

items.title: Public Participation and Advocacy Groups
items.summary: The speakers encouraged participation via email and Zoom while highlighting the efforts of the Charter Study Commission and advocacy groups like Safe Medford and Housing Medford.

items.title: Governance Strategy and Political Optics
items.summary: Callahan described her use of volunteer advisory teams and community listening sessions to ensure her votes align with her values rather than political optics.
